# 49 - Focus Booster

> 49 - Focus Booster is a focus-training game for iPhone and Android built on the Schulte table, a classic attention exercise. Players find the numbers 1 to 49, shuffled on a 7 × 7 board, in order and as fast as they can. A game takes about a minute. A minute a day lets players practise sustained attention, faster reading (wider eye span), visual search and calm under pressure, and see their progress in Insights. It is a game, not a medical product. It is free to play with ads between games. Premium (weekly, monthly, yearly with a free week, or lifetime) removes the ads. Nothing is locked behind a purchase. Out now, free on the App Store for iPhone. On Android it is in testing on Google Play, and anyone can join. Made by Artur Pereć (https://www.linkedin.com/in/arturperec/).

Key facts:

- Platforms: iPhone with iOS 17 or later, free on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823997426. Android 9 or later, in testing on Google Play that anyone can join: https://49game.github.io/#android
- Game types: Classic (one board, best time), Endless (boards keep coming, scored by pace), Beat the Clock (every find adds time, every miss costs time).
- Orders: count up from 1 to 49, down from 49 to 1, or in random order, in every game type.
- Styles: Normal (a plain time trial), Competitive (points, combos and a multiplier up to ×3), Relax (effects and sounds, without points, records or ranks, and 3 free hints a game).
- Boards: Numbers from 3 × 3 to 11 × 11 (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 11 tiles a side), Red & Black (count red up and black down) from 5 × 5 to 7 × 7, and Letters from 5 × 5 to 7 × 7 (A to Y on 5 × 5, then capital and small letters).
- Competitive scoring: 100 points per number plus a speed bonus of up to 50 that shrinks with time. ×2 from a combo of 5, ×3 from 15. The combo is lost when its timer runs out and halved by a wrong tap, which never takes points away.
- Daily Challenge: the same board for everyone each day. Most days the board itself moves or changes its look (for example Spin Up, a board that turns faster with every find, or fog, blinds and reshuffles), with a still version for players who use Reduce Motion. Special days bring a board of their own: a heart on Valentine's Day (69 Mode), a pumpkin on Halloween (Jack-o'-Lantern), a ball of yarn on Cat Day (17 February and 8 August) and a bone on Dog Day (1 July and 26 August). On April Fools' Day there is Totally Normal Mode.
- Every day: three quests, XP and levels, a streak with streak freezes and an optional reminder.
- Ranks from Rookie to Legend for every mode, direction, style and board.
- 578 achievements in 20 groups, tiered on eight medals from bronze to prismatic.
- 100 Game Center leaderboards: fastest time and most points by board and direction, for today, this week, this month and all time. The Daily has its own board, where a player's best attempt counts.
- Multiplayer: 1 v 1, 2 v 2 and group rooms with Race, Points battle, Knockout and Ghost race, all on the same board for everyone, plus Steal (one board, live: whoever taps a number first scores it). Friends join with a five-character room code, a QR code or a link, with a nickname per game. A lobby lists public rooms, quick pairing finds an opponent, and ranked games have their own ratings. Guest mode lets friends play on one phone.
- Hints: 3 free a day, and more after every 10 games. Each adds 5 seconds, so hints never set a record.
- Insights: blind spots on the board, time of day, rhythm and the most common mistakes. After every game, one sentence on the biggest improvement.
- Eight looks (Classic, Focus, Neon Arcade, Zen Ink, Pit Lane, Candy Pop, Blossom, Black Gold), a theme builder and 42 sound styles. App icons: the standard icon, Arcade, Pit Lane and Blossom.
- Accessibility: VoiceOver, Reduce Motion, Bold Text, Audio Graphs, Color vision (colors that stay easy to tell apart), Hide found numbers, and switches for confetti, flashes and haptics.
- Languages: English, Polish, German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Korean.
- Data: games and stats are kept on the iPhone and sync through the player's own iCloud, and there is no account to create. Multiplayer rooms and player profiles (nickname, ratings, recent games) are stored in iCloud so other players can see them. Anonymous usage statistics (TelemetryDeck, no names or game history) can be turned off in Settings. Game Center is optional. The free version shows ads from Google AdMob. New features come first to the open TestFlight beta: https://testflight.apple.com/join/G4XsUyyB.
- Support: contact49game@icloud.com (or https://github.com/49Game/49game.github.io/issues)
